name: Bishlam
title: Persian official who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem
summary: Bishlam was one of the Persian officials or settlers in Samaria who helped write a letter of complaint to King Artaxerxes to stop the Jews from rebuilding Jerusalem. He is mentioned in Ezra 4:7 as one of the senders of the letter. His role was limited, but he represented local opposition to the return and restoration of the Jews.

keyEvents.title: Letter of Complaint Against Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Bishlam was one of the senders of a letter to King Artaxerxes in which they complained that the Jews were rebuilding Jerusalem, claiming that the city had historically been rebellious.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to the Rebuilding
keyEvents.description: The letter that Bilsan helped send led the king to order a halt to the rebuilding work in Jerusalem, which significantly delayed the Jews' project.

keyEvents.title: Cooperation with Rehum and Shimshai
keyEvents.description: Bilshan acted together with the chancellor Rehum and the scribe Shimshai, as well as other officials in the province beyond the river, in their joint opposition to the Jews.

keyEvents.title: Consequences of the Letter
keyEvents.description: As a result of the letter and the king's response, the rebuilding of the temple and the city was forcibly stopped with weapons until the second year of King Darius' reign.
